spec.title: Checks failing now
spec.description: Health checks currently reporting 0, across every node in scope. Which ones is in the table below.

spec.title: Nodes failing, by check
spec.description: How many nodes are failing each check, over time. One row per check kind — that set is fixed by the agent code, so this panel stays readable however large the fleet gets. Green 'ok' = every node in scope passing; a coloured segment shows the number of nodes failing.

spec.title: Failures in this time range
spec.description: Every node/check pair that failed at least once in the selected range, and for how long. Sampled at 1-minute resolution, so a blip shorter than a minute still shows as 1.

defaults.noValue: ✓  no health check failed in this time range

spec.title: Egress throughput per exit
spec.description: Measured egress bandwidth (passive live traffic, or an active probe on an idle link). The dashed line is the configured floor (250 KiB/s default); a sustained collapse below it auto-suspends the exit from the LB.

spec.title: Active egress method
spec.description: Which egress each exit is currently using (warp / direct). Differs from the preferred egress while failed over.

spec.title: Exits out of rotation
spec.description: Master↔exit tunnels mihomo currently has marked down. These tunnels are userspace mihomo proxies, not kernel WireGuard, so no wg_* panel covers them — this is their only view. Non-zero means wg-best is not routing client traffic to that exit. Counts only the tier that carries traffic: a dual-transport exit also renders a standby proxy that is in no group and never probed, so its reading is meaningless here and would sit permanently non-zero.

spec.expr: sum(wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive == 0 and on(exit) wgfleet_agent_exit_held_out) or vector(0)

spec.title: Held out by our probe
spec.description: Of the exits above, how many the master agent's own multi-destination probe took out — it requires reachability across four independent destinations, so it catches a censored-but-"healthy" exit that answers mihomo's single lightweight check. The rest were dropped by mihomo's own group check.

spec.title: Exit in rotation, over time
spec.description: When each exit was actually carrying client traffic. This is the panel that answers "why did it drop out and when" — before it existed that had to be reconstructed from the master agent's journal. Standby-transport proxies are excluded — they are configured but in no group, so "in rotation" does not apply to them.

spec.title: master↔exit tunnel delay
spec.description: Last url-test delay per tunnel, as mihomo measured it. A failed measurement is ABSENT, not zero — a dead tunnel must never render as the fastest one.

spec.title: Client UDP black holes
spec.description: UDP ports this master holds a socket on that are NOT declared, so mihomo cannot open a transparent reply socket for them and client traffic to those ports gets no replies. Anything above zero is a silent outage for that port: requests leave, nothing returns.

spec.expr: count(wgfleet_agent_udp_return_socket == 0 and on(node, port) wgfleet_agent_udp_return_known == 0) or vector(0)

spec.title: UDP reply socket possible, by port
spec.description: 1 = a TPROXY reply socket can still be opened for that destination port; 0 = a socket this host already holds makes it impossible. Port 443 sitting at 0 is the client AmneziaWG interface holding it, which is why client QUIC had no return path from 2026-08-28.

spec.title: Held out by the multi-destination probe
spec.description: The CAUSE behind the rotation panel: red means the master agent's probe judged this exit unable to reach enough independent destinations and is holding it out. mihomo's own weaker check would put such an exit straight back, so the agent re-probes every held-out member each pass to keep the stricter verdict in force.

spec.title: Config drift (resources repaired)
spec.description: Resources the agent had to repair while the desired spec was unchanged — i.e. real drift or external tampering.

spec.title: Active transport
spec.description: Which master↔exit transport each exit is currently routed over (awg / reality-xhttp). Switch it per node on its detail page.

spec.title: Standby transport usable
spec.description: Whether each dual-transport exit's INACTIVE transport — the one an operator would switch it onto — can actually reach the internet. Absent means never measured, which is not the same as healthy: an untested mihomo proxy reports alive=1 by default, so before this was probed the fleet showed a confident green on no evidence. The switch is an emergency move, made exactly when the active path is blocked.

defaults.noValue: no dual-transport exit has been measured yet

spec.title: Client-VLESS inbound down
spec.description: Masters whose client-facing VLESS/REALITY inbound self-check is failing. Non-zero means DPI-throttled clients can't fall back to the VLESS transport.

spec.title: VLESS clients issued
spec.description: Total VLESS/REALITY client credentials issued across selected masters.

spec.title: VLESS clients per master
spec.description: Issued VLESS/REALITY client count per master over time.

spec.title: Probes that never succeeded
spec.description: Scheduled probes that have run at least once but have NEVER produced a result. Non-zero means the probe is dead while the node still reports Ready: it degrades to a default on failure, so nothing else surfaces it.

spec.title: Probes stale > 7d
spec.description: Probes that succeeded once but not in the last 7 days. Both probes run about daily, so this is a probe that started failing and kept the last-good value in force ever since.

spec.title: Time since last successful probe run
spec.description: Per node and probe: how long ago the probe last SUCCEEDED. A probe that has never succeeded shows an absurd age (measured from epoch) and colors red — that is the signature to look for. Rows appear only once a probe has actually run on that node.
